# SB-1008: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet
Revision: Rev D
Plant: P1, line P1-L2
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-RR01

## Hazard description
An arc flash event occurred during a maintenance access of the induction power cabinet serving the ring rolling radial ring rolling mill indicated by equipment id EQ-P1-L2-RR01. The event created an unplanned release of energy within the cabinet, presenting thermal and blast hazards and producing conductive debris and molten material. Personnel in the immediate vicinity experienced near-miss exposure to hot debris and bright flash without appropriate proximity barriers. The potential exists for serious injury to operators, maintenance technicians, and support personnel when work is performed at or near the cabinet without established electrical safety boundaries, documented isolation, and verified absence of hazardous energy.

Background: The induction power cabinet supplies rolling drive equipment for the radial ring rolling mill. The maximum ring outer diameter for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) is 995 mm. The cabinet contains power conversion and switching components that require controlled access and strict lockout procedures during any work that could expose personnel to live conductors or stored energy. Recent procedural drift and informal bypassing of entry controls were identified as contributing factors to the recent arc flash event.

Step rationale: Arc flash hazards are mitigated by guaranteeing that personnel are not exposed to live parts, that panels are maintained in a condition that prevents inadvertent contact, and that testing or troubleshooting activities are performed only under documented protective protocols. This bulletin clarifies required controls, required documentation, and acceptable work practices to prevent recurrence.

## Affected equipment
- Induction power cabinet serving the radial ring rolling mill identified as EQ-P1-L2-RR01.
- Associated control cabinets and access points that share electrical distribution or grounding paths with the induction power cabinet.
- Work areas adjacent to the cabinet where personnel perform setup, inspection, or troubleshooting activities.

Scope: This bulletin applies to all personnel who operate, maintain, inspect, or otherwise enter the area around EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Contractors and temporary workers performing tasks in the same space are included and must comply with the controls outlined below.

Related documents: ECN-2026-009, SOP-P1-L2-03, SOP-P1-L2-05.

## Required controls
Access control
- Do not access the induction power cabinet unless work is authorized and an electrical hazard assessment has been completed and documented.
- Establish and maintain a physical perimeter around the cabinet when energized activities are in progress. Use signage and barriers to prevent unauthorized entry.

Energy isolation and verification
- Before any maintenance, testing, or intrusive inspection, complete isolation using the established lockout process. Ensure locks and tags are applied by authorized personnel only.
- Verify de-energization using the prescribed test methodology in the applicable standard operating procedure. Record verification results in the job safety record.

Personal protective equipment and clothing
- Use PPE selected based on the documented hazard assessment for the task and the specific cabinet exposure. PPE must be inspected prior to use and stored in a controlled location when not in service.

Work authorization and supervision
- All work that could expose personnel to energized parts requires prior written authorization and direct supervision by an authorized electrical supervisor.
- Permit-to-work documentation must be completed in full and made available on site for the duration of the activity.

Procedures and training
- Only personnel trained and authorized per SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05 may perform electrical maintenance, troubleshooting, or testing on the cabinet and related equipment.
- Refresher training is required when procedural changes, equipment modifications, or installation changes documented in ECN-2026-009 are implemented.

Maintenance and preventive measures
- Do not bypass or modify protective devices without documented engineering approval and revision control captured in ECN-2026-009.
- Maintain cabinet access panels and barriers in original configuration. Any repairs must be carried out under lockout and documented in the maintenance record.

Examples of unacceptable practices
- Performing continuity checks or component testing with panels open and without verified isolation.
- Temporarily defeating interlocks or grounding connections to expedite a troubleshooting activity.
- Allowing non-authorized personnel to stand inside the established perimeter during energized work.

Records to keep
- Job safety assessment and hazard analysis for each access event, retained with the permit-to-work document.
- Lockout tagout records showing isolation points, lock identifiers, and verification signatures.
- De-energization verification results including tester identity and calibration evidence.
- Incident and near-miss reports filed for any deviation or unexpected event during work on or near the induction power cabinet.
- Training and authorization records demonstrating compliance with SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05.
- Any engineering change notices or design modifications recorded in ECN-2026-009 that affect cabinet function or protective settings.

Record retention: Keep the above records in the plant document control system as specified by site retention policy and attach records to the equipment file for EQ-P1-L2-RR01.

## Effective date
This bulletin is effective immediately upon release and remains in force until superseded. Implement required controls for all activities involving the induction power cabinet for EQ-P1-L2-RR01 and related systems. Review the related documents ECN-2026-009, SOP-P1-L2-03, and SOP-P1-L2-05 for procedural detail and specific authorizations. Supervisors must verify compliance through spot checks and the maintenance review process and must escalate any nonconformance to plant management for corrective action.

Action items for supervisors
- Brief affected teams on the controls and ensure permits and records are in place before any work is performed.
- Coordinate with engineering for any modifications referenced in ECN-2026-009 prior to returning equipment to service.
- Ensure training and authorization per SOP-P1-L2-03 and SOP-P1-L2-05 are current for personnel assigned to tasks involving the cabinet.

Follow-up: A formal review will be scheduled to assess compliance and to determine if additional controls or engineering changes are required. Document findings and corrective actions in the plant safety review file and attach to EQ-P1-L2-RR01 records.
